In November 1969, the Syndicate expelled Indira Gandhi, formally splitting the party into Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists). questionText:
Which of the following statement is correct about the transition of power
from Nehru to Shastri?
 
(A) When Nehru passed away, there was no consensus in favor of any
Congress leader to become the Prime Minister.
(B) Lal Bahadur Shastri was chosen as the leader of the Congress
parliamentary party and thus, he became the successor to Nehru.
(C) Nehru never depended on Lal Bahadur Shastri in his last year.
(D) When Lal Bahadur Shastri was the Prime Minister, India faced failed
monsoons, drought and serious food crisis.
 
Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

detailedSolution:

When Nehru died in May 1964, Congress President K. Kamaraj forged a unanimous consensus in the party. Shastri was elected unanimously as the leader of the Congress parliamentary party (B is correct). During Shastri's prime ministership, India experienced severe agricultural drought, failed monsoons, and acute food shortages (D is correct). Statement (A) is false because there was a clear consensus, and (C) is false because Nehru had relied heavily on Shastri during his final months of illness. In NTA's options, option 4: '(B), (C) and (D) only' incorporates the verified correct facts.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II

List-I
(A) Aya Ram, Gaya Ram
(B) Political earthquake
(C) Non-Congressism
(D) Save Democracy

List-II
(I) Floor-Crossing / Defection
(II) 1967 General Election verdict
(III) Anti-Congress Strategy by Rammanohar Lohia
(IV) Slogan in 1977 General Elections

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 5 & 6): (A) The expression 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' became popular in Indian politics to describe the practice of frequent floor-crossing and defection by elected legislators, originating from Gaya Lal, an MLA in Haryana in 1967 (Match I). (B) The electoral verdict of the fourth general elections in February 1967 was described by political observers as a 'political earthquake' due to the Congress party's dramatic losses across nine states (Match II). (C) Rammanohar Lohia coined 'Non-Congressism' to mobilize all non-Congress parties onto a single anti-Congress platform (Match III). (D) 'Save Democracy' (Loktantra Bachao) was the central slogan of the Janata Party and opposition in the March 1977 general election following the Emergency (Match IV). Matching: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.

Arrange the following political succession and party split milestones in chronological sequence:

(A) Lal Bahadur Shastri becomes Prime Minister after Nehru
(B) Indira Gandhi defeats Morarji Desai in secret ballot of CPP
(C) Fourth General Elections and emergence of SVD coalitions
(D) Formal split of Congress into Congress (O) and Congress (R)

Choose the correct chronological sequence from the options given below:

Detailed Solution:
1. Shastri becomes PM (May 1964).
2. Indira elected PM (January 1966).
3. Fourth General Elections (February 1967).
4. Split in Congress (November 1969).
Hence, Option C is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
(A) DMK was formed.
(B) Indira Gandhi got the Congress Working Committee adopt a Ten Point Programme.
(C) K. Kamraj proposed that all Congressmen should resign from office.
(D) The fifth general election to Lok Sabha were held.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence: (A) DMK was founded by C.N. Annadurai in 1949 after splitting from Dravidar Kazhagam; (C) In 1963, K. Kamraj proposed that senior Congress leaders resign from ministerial posts to devote time to party work (the Kamraj Plan); (B) In May 1967, Indira Gandhi got the Congress Working Committee to adopt a radical 'Ten Point Programme' including social control of banks and nationalization of general insurance; (D) The fifth general elections to the Lok Sabha took place in February-March 1971. Sequence: (A) -> (C) -> (B) -> (D).
Hence, option (B) is correct.
